name: The Alienation Playbook
description: The recurring tactic patterns documented across thousands of high-conflict custody cases. Different families, same script. Recognizing the pattern early — and documenting it factually — is the counter.
principle: Expose patterns, never people. Individual records belong in YOUR private, dated log — and in court. Public accusation helps the alienator; organized documentation helps your child.

patterns.name: Access Interference
signs: Visits cancelled without valid reason, often last-minute
Child reported 'sick' or 'busy' on exchange days but fine for school
'He doesn't want to come, and I'm not going to force him'
patterns.counter: Log every attempt: date, time, reason given, witnesses. School attendance that week. One missed visit is nothing; forty logged ones are a pattern a judge can act on.

patterns.name: Information Gatekeeping
patterns.counter: Request information in writing on a schedule; log request date vs. disclosure date vs. event date. The gap is the evidence.

patterns.name: Therapeutic Manipulation
signs: Therapy used to delay or condition access
Child's statements in therapy mirror one parent's exact phrases
'I have absolutely no respect for him' delivered to professionals
patterns.counter: Provide the professional your documented record early and in writing. Compare therapist recommendations against court orders. Professionals believe records, not arguments.

patterns.name: Narrative Control
signs: 'He never does anything. He can't cook. He can't clean.'
Reports to authorities timed to litigation
Threats: 'If you call or text, I'll file a restraining order and say you grabbed me'
Different versions of events to different professionals
patterns.counter: Never argue the story — document the contradictions side by side (claim, source, date vs. record). Her story changes every time she tells it; the record tells it the same way twice.

patterns.name: Child Instrumentalization
signs: Child repeats adult legal vocabulary ('you violated the parenting agreement')
Litigation details shared with the child
patterns.counter: Write the child's exact words verbatim with date and context. Borrowed language is a recognized marker professionals look for. Never interrogate the child; just record.

first_72_hours: Start a dated log tonight — even a notes app
Save every message; screenshot with timestamps
Respond BIFF: Brief, Informative, Friendly, Firm — write every message as if a judge will read it
Do not vent publicly or to the child
